observations: What I read: the whole prepared request (base.script with all 23 panels 01-1..06-4, the decisions, dialoguePolicy and dialogueInstructions), works/auto-6294ee8a2094/source/original.txt in full, works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/source-coverage.json in full, docs/REVISION-AND-REVIEWS.md in full, and AGENTS.md as supplied in the project instructions. For docs/PROMPTS.md I only searched for the lines about script, review and dialogueReview; I did not read it in full. I also read the previous response script-all-r5.json for context. No artwork exists at this stage, so I saw and inspected no images. Every file was readable. Order: I read the lettered lines alone in panel order first, then compared them with the source and checked the scene and production fields.

Reading the lettering alone, every exchange holds up. 'the rest' (01-3) points back to Meera's list in 01-2. 'here' (02-2) points to the laptop in 02-1. Meera's 'And our team...' (02-3) follows straight on from Ananya in 02-2. Each question is answered in the next panel: 03-1 to 03-2 ('Of course'), 03-2 to 03-3 ('Yes, please'), 04-1 to 04-2, and 05-2 to 05-3 ('That's the idea'). 'your concerns' (04-4) points back to 04-2. All lines and captions match the source word for word. The only change is 01-2, where Meera's single line is split into two balloons by the same speaker at the ellipsis. No turns are merged across another speaker, and the voices fit: Ananya calm and decisive, Meera helpful and polite, Ravi casual and warm.

The r5 stethoscope issue is fixed, and I checked it myself rather than relying on the change summary. All five sections where Ananya appears (clinic-morning, onboarding, reception, consultation, closing) now say 'stethoscope worn around her neck (not in use)'. The cast description ties it to every scene where she wears the white coat, which matches those sections, since none of them drops the coat. The specialist's vision costume now includes the stethoscope, so it matches his cast description. The 04-4 scene now reads 'no instruments in use' with the stethoscope staying around her neck. No panel shows an examination, test result, diagnosis or prescription. The stethoscope is a costume item, not a medical claim.

Product roles and vision separation follow the source. Practice is on the laptop for the clinic (02-1), Care on the staff phone (02-3) and Health on Ravi's own phone for patients (05-1, 05-2). The labels name only products the source already describes, and the coverage file records them as supplements. Only 06-2 and 06-3 carry 'WELBUK VISION' and the pale-blue vignette. 06-1 keeps the conditional 'may', and 06-4 is explicitly back in the present with no vignette. Screens show only abstract blocks and icons. 03-3 rules out ID cards and written papers, as the source's 'no actual identifying data' requires. I found no invented features and no real data.

Props, hands and screen direction are consistent. Ravi's bag is strap-held in 03-1 and 03-4, set on the floor in 04-1 and 04-4, and back on his shoulder in 05-1 and 05-4. His phone goes from pocket to right hand (05-1), both hands (05-2), left hand (05-4) and his lap (06-1). Meera holds the staff phone in her right hand in 02-3, 02-4 and 06-4. No hand has two tasks at once. Screen direction stays within each scene: Ravi left / Meera right on page 3, Ananya left / Ravi right across 04-1 to 04-4, and Meera left / Ravi right across 05-1 to 05-3. Pages 3 and 5 flip the Meera/Ravi sides. That is acceptable because page 4 comes between them and 05-1 is a fresh corner shot, but the storyboard review should confirm it reads naturally.

Minor, not blocking: in 05-2 ravi-phone is heldBy 'ravi.right' while both hands hold it, and in 06-3 family-tablet is heldBy 'partner.left' while both hands hold it. The hands fields make the two-handed grip clear, but the heldBy values could list both hands if the schema allows. Also not blocking: 02-1 is a hands-only close shot, so the stethoscope will probably not be visible there, which is fine.

issues.problem: Panel 05-4 takes the wrong section. The script defines a 'departure' section for exactly this beat ('The end of the same visit: Ravi leaves the clinic reassured'; location 'Clinic entrance from the street side, morning sun'; Ravi's costume only). However, 05-4 sets no panel-level section, so it inherits page 05's 'reception' section, and no panel uses 'departure' at all. As a result, the section data given to the renderer for 05-4 says 'The same reception desk, now tidy with a desktop monitor... waiting chairs', while the scene says 'Outside the clinic entrance... steps out onto the street'. The inherited section also lists costumes for Ananya and Meera, who are not in the panel. This is the same kind of conflicting instruction as the r5 stethoscope issue and risks an indoor or wrongly populated render. Fix: add "section": "departure" to panel 05-4 (or remove the unused section and rewrite the reception location, but linking departure is the obvious intent). Then re-prepare and re-review.
issues.location: pages[05].panels[05-4] (no section field; inherits pages[05].section 'reception') vs sections.departure (defined but unused)

panels.observation: The source caption 'A busy day at Dr. Ananya's clinic.' is kept word for word. It introduces Ananya by name and sets up the 'busy' premise that Meera's complaint in 01-2 depends on.
Meera's single source line is split at the ellipsis into two balloons by the same speaker, with nothing in between. The list (appointments, details, follow-ups) gives 'everything' its referent.
Ananya's line is word for word. 'the rest' depends on the paperwork list in 01-2 just before it, and her looking at the desk gives the reason she decides to act.
The onboarding caption is word for word, and evening light marks the time change. The added Practice label names the source's 'laptop view of Welbuk Practice' without claiming any feature.
The line is word for word. 'here' refers to the laptop setup in 02-1, and her considering team roles (from the source) sets up 02-3.
Meera's 'And our team...' is word for word and continues Ananya's 02-2 line directly, with no other speaker between them. The Care label matches the source's 'staff phone displaying Welbuk Care'.
'One team. Better coordination.' is word for word and sums up 02-2 and 02-3. Meera's silent nod is a reaction added for the manga, not a dropped line.
Ravi's greeting and request are word for word. His request to see the doctor is what Meera's 'Of course' in 03-2 answers.
The line is word for word. It answers 03-1 and asks the consent question that 03-3 replies to, so consent comes before any data is entered, as the source requires.
'Yes, please.' answers the 03-2 consent question directly. Meera types into blank fields only, with no ID cards or written papers, matching 'no actual identifying data'.
'You're all set, Ravi. Please have a seat.' is word for word. Using his name follows naturally from the registration, and the gesture to the chairs leads into page 4.
Ananya's greeting is word for word, and the same costumes show this is the same visit after the place change. 'Tell me what brings you in' is the question 04-2 answers.
'I've been feeling tired lately.' answers 04-1 word for word as the source's routine concern. No diagnosis or advice is written or drawn.
The caption is word for word and is backed by the closed laptop and an attentive, silent listener. It comments on the 04-1/04-2 exchange without adding medical content.

The line is word for word, and 'your concerns' refers back to 04-2. The scene now says no instruments are in use, with the stethoscope only worn, so the r5 conflict is resolved and no treatment advice appears.
Meera's line is word for word and keeps the careful 'designed to help'. The return to reception places it after the consultation in time.

Ravi's question is word for word and depends on Meera's explanation in 05-1. The abstract calendar and heart cards stand in for the source's 'appointments and health information' without showing any data.
'That's the idea' answers the 05-2 question directly. 'what is available to you' is kept word for word, so no unlaunched feature is implied.
The caption is word for word, and Ravi leaving with his phone and bag shows the source's 'reassured'. The panel's section assignment is wrong (see issue), but the dialogue itself is correct.
The caption is word for word and keeps the conditional 'may'. The train window carries the change of time and place without presenting the vision as current.
The 'WELBUK VISION' label the source asks for and the caption are word for word inside the vignette. The symbolic specialist and the dotted links do not suggest a launched referral feature.
The caption is word for word. The repeated vision label and the vignette keep the family wellness app conceptual, with abstract icons only.
The three product labels and the final caption are word for word. The present-day group shot ties Practice, Care and Health back to Ananya, Meera and Ravi as set up in 02-1, 02-3 and 05-2.
